title: Trust Center: Data Flow & Evidence Guide (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note is a working draft intended to consolidate the pieces we surface to customers in the Trust Center about how audit evidence is produced, mapped to questionnaire responses, and exported to customer SIEMs. It focuses on three practical slices: RBAC v2 signal coverage, audit-log schema and retention artifacts, and the evidence automation path (how to generate artifact bundles).

Audience:
Customer security reviewers, SOC engineers, solutions engineers, and the product security lead preparing Trust Center copy or a customer package.

Executive summary (two lines):
- Redwood generates structured audit events for auth, model-serving actions, config changes, and data-plane access.
- We provide downloadable evidence bundles and a combination of push (S3/FTP) and pull (SIEM API) export options; automation ties questionnaire answers to named artifacts.

Key components described below:
1) RBAC v2: what we record and where
- Scope: role definitions, role bindings, permission changes, temporary elevations, and service-to-service credentials.
- Evidence types: role-change events (who changed which permission), role-binding snapshots (periodic export of current bindings), recent-policy-diff (compressed patch for last 30 days).
- How we present it: for questionnaire items asking about privilege change controls, reference artifact names: rbac-v2-bindings-YYYYMMDD.csv and rbac-policy-diffs-30d.jsonl.

2) Audit log schema (short reference)
- Format: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with stable top-level fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, actor_id, actor_type, principal_ip, action_type, resource_path, resource_type, request_id, outcome, metadata (flat map).
- Action families: AUTH (login, token-issue, mfa), IAM (role.create/role.update/role.bind), CONFIG (service-config.override), SERVE (model.invoke, model.deploy, kvcache.miss/hit), DATA_ACCESS (dataset.read, dataset.write).
- Retention and signing: logs are retained per customer retention policy (default 90 days hosted API) and signed by HMAC keys stored in KMS; evidence bundle includes signature manifests.

3) SIEM export mapping and delivery patterns
- Supported outputs: syslog (CEF/LEEF), S3 buckets (ndjson), and HTTPS webhook for SIEM ingestion.
- Mapping doc: we include a canonical field map (event_id -> external_id, timestamp_utc -> event_time, outcome -> severity) plus an example CEF mapping for priority fields.
- Delivery modes: push-to-customer-s3 (recommended for large volumes), pull-api (customer-initiated), and partner-forward (Splunk HTTP Event Collector token).

4) Evidence automation pipeline (how to assemble a customer package)
- Trigger points: manual request (support portal), automated on-boarding checkpoint, or scheduled quarterly package.
- Components included: rbac snapshots, signed audit-log slice (range requested), config-export (service, network ACLs), vulnerability scan summary (last 30 days), and a manifest.json that lists artifact checksums and signatures.
- Automation stub: a Lambda-style job (jira: JIRA-SEC-412) that builds bundles and drops to the customer-requested S3 path; PR reference: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-schema/pull/88.

5) Questionnaire answer templates (short-form examples)
- Q: "How do you detect privilege escalation events?"
  A: "Privilege changes are logged via our IAM events stream (IAM.role.update, IAM.role.binding) with actor, timestamp, and before/after snapshots. We retain events for 90 days by default and provide signed exports on request. See artifact: rbac-v2-bindings-2024-11-01.csv."
- Q: "Can we stream audit logs into our SIEM?"
  A: "Yes — we support push to S3 and HTTPS push to SIEM endpoints (CEF/LEEF mappings available). Recommended method for high-volume customers is S3 export with lifecycle policies on your side."

6) Typical customer evidence package (example manifest)
- files: ["rbac-v2-bindings-2024-11-01.csv","audit-slice-2024-10-01_2024-11-01.ndjson.gz","config-export-2024-11-01.json","signature-manifest-2024-11-01.sig"]
- notes: each artifact includes signer id and checksum.

7) Known gaps & risk notes (what to be honest about)
- We do not currently export raw model token-level content by default; data-plane event descriptions are redacted to avoid PII exfiltration risk.
- Retention limits depend on plan; Dedicated customers can request extended retention and private deployments have deploy-time retention controls.

8) Next steps & owners (short checklist)
- Finalize canonical field map and publish as Confluence page (owner: Elliot Park, due: 2024-12-10).
- Add CEF example to Trust Center docs and include a sample Splunk HEC config (owner: Nayla Ortiz, due: 2024-12-17).
- Wire evidence automation lambda into support portal flow and test with 2 pilot customers (owner: Marcus Li, due: 2025-01-10).

Appendix: quick links and references
- Audit schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-schema/pull/88
- Confluence: /infr/TC-dataflow-v1
- Jira epic: JIRA-SEC-412

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a working draft intended to be customer-facing but reviewed by product security and legal before publishing. Feedback: please flag any over-sharing of raw request payloads or missing compliance statements (HIPAA, SOC2 language).
